Yes. Here is the practical implementation table.

This is the **Missouri-first FieldLog rule/check matrix**. These are the items your app should check, display, tag with source, and include in audit/export output.

Primary source basis: Missouri’s recordkeeping rule, **2 CSR 70-25.120**, says certified commercial applicators/employers must keep records for all pesticide uses, while certified noncommercial applicators and public operators/employers must keep records for restricted-use pesticides. Records must be completed within three business days, kept three years, available for inspection, and contain the listed application fields.  RSMo §281.035 gives the statutory commercial-applicator recordkeeping duty and three-year retention requirement.  FIFRA makes it unlawful to use a registered pesticide inconsistently with its labeling, which is why label-related checks should be flagged as “review required,” not treated as automatically resolved by record completeness.

| -: | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
|  1 | Applicator category                           | Determine whether the record is for certified commercial, certified noncommercial, public operator, private applicator, noncertified applicator, RUP applicator, technician, or trainee | Every record                                                                       | `NEEDS_REVIEW` if unknown                                                 | `2_CSR_70_25_120`, `RSMO_281_035`                               |
|  2 | Commercial applicator record duty             | Certified commercial applicator or employer must maintain records for pesticide applications                                                                                            | Commercial application                                                             | `NEEDS_REVIEW` if app cannot identify responsible recordkeeper            | `RSMO_281_035`, `2_CSR_70_25_120`                               |

|  4 | Pesticide type / RUP status                   | Whether product is restricted-use pesticide, general-use, minimum-risk, or unknown                                                                                                      | Every product                                                                      | `LABEL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` if unknown                                  | `2_CSR_70_25_120`, `FIFRA_LABELING`                             |

For your current build, do **not** try to implement all 82 as hard blockers. That would make the app brittle and annoying.

Use this priority split.

| Priority | Implement as                      | Checks                                              |
| -------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| P0       | Hard required-field checks        | 8, 9, 16–25, 27, 29–30, 32, 37–40, 44, 46–48, 52–55 |
| P0       | Timing/retention checks           | 5, 6                                                |
| P0       | Source tagging                    | 80                                                  |
| P0       | Review/export integrity           | 73–79, 81–82                                        |
| P1       | Conditional applicability checks  | 1–4, 10–15, 26, 33–34, 41–43, 45                    |
| P1       | Label verification flags          | 35–36, 56–64                                        |
| P2       | Tank mix refinement               | 65–67                                               |
| P2       | Noncertified supervision workflow | 68–71                                               |
| P2       | GPS/weather evidence quality      | 49–51, 72                                           |

The immediate hackathon/demo version should check this minimum set:

| Minimum demo check                                       | Failure status           |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| Application date missing                                 | `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` |
| Start time missing                                       | `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` |
| End time missing                                         | `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` |
| Certified applicator name/license missing                | `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` |
| Requester name/address missing                           | `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` |
| Application site missing                                 | `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` |
| Area treated missing                                     | `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` |
| Crop/site/commodity missing when applicable              | `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` |
| Target pest missing                                      | `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` |
| Product trade name missing                               | `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` |
| EPA registration number missing                          | `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` |
| Rate/amount missing                                      | `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` |
| Outdoor temperature missing                              | `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` |
| Outdoor wind speed missing                               | `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` |
| Outdoor wind direction missing                           | `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` |
| Record submitted after three business days               | `WARNING`                |
| Retain-until date missing                                | derive automatically     |
| Source citation missing on any result                    | internal dev failure     |
| Approval attempted with unresolved required-field errors | block normal approval    |
| Export missing checklist/timeline/disclaimer             | block export             |

The sharp product language is:

**FieldLog automates pesticide compliance tracking for recordkeeping. It checks required Missouri record fields, timing, retention, correction history, and audit readiness. It separately flags label-dependent issues for human review.**

That is the line between a strong compliance product and an unsafe legal oracle.
